about.title: Secure key exchange
body: Your phone and your contact's phone create matching encryption keys directly with each other — nothing secret is sent in plain text.
The server only relays encrypted data between you. It never sees your private keys or can read your messages.
This step sets up end-to-end encryption before you verify the connection.

waiting.title: Waiting for your contact
body: Your contact needs to open the chat and finish the same setup on their phone.
Until they do, your app waits here — that's normal and your keys stay only on your device.
If it takes a while, ask them to open the app and keep this screen open.

about.title: Safety check
body: You see a safety number and emoji pattern derived from both encryption keys. Your contact sees the same pattern on their phone.
Compare them out loud or side by side. If they match, you're talking directly to each other — not through someone in the middle.
This protects against someone swapping keys on the server (a man-in-the-middle attack).

mismatch.title: Patterns don't match
body: If the numbers or emoji don't match, do not trust this chat. Someone may be intercepting the connection.
Stop here. Start a new chat with your contact over a channel you both trust, and compare again.
Tap "Leave and burn this chat" to destroy this session. Do not keep messaging on a mismatched fingerprint.

about.title: What burning destroys
body: Burning this chat permanently removes the session on the server and clears encryption keys on your device.
Your message history and the link between you and this contact for this chat are erased. Your contact's app is notified so their side is cleared too.
This cannot be undone. It affects only this one-to-one chat — not your other chats, rooms, or wallet.

create.title: Creating a room
body: A room is a shared encrypted space with its own invite link. You become the owner and control who can join.
Set a password or require owner approval so strangers cannot enter with only the link.
Room data on the server has a time limit and disappears when the room is burned or expires.

join.title: Joining a room
body: You opened an invite link. The owner decides how joining works: enter the password, or send a request and wait for approval.
The password is never sent in plain text — it protects access to the room's encrypted keys.
If the link expired or was revoked, ask the owner for a new invite.

about.title: Home: chats and rooms
body: This screen lists your one-to-one chats and encrypted rooms. Everything here is temporary and disappears when a chat is burned or its time limit ends.
Search starts a new encrypted chat. Create Room makes a shared space with an invite link.
If the list is suddenly empty after you had chats, the relay may have lost session data — that is expected for an ephemeral store, not a silent wipe of your wallet.

about.title: Encrypted chat
body: Messages are encrypted on your device. The server only relays ciphertext and cannot read them.
Telegram Premium (star) is the Telegram subscription. A BURN badge is your staking tier on TON — they are not the same.
Burn chat destroys this conversation and its keys. It does not burn BURN tokens.

about.title: Encrypted files
body: Files are encrypted on your device before upload. The server stores an opaque blob with a short lifetime.
You can cancel an upload before it finishes. After send, the file follows the same burn and TTL rules as messages.
Do not assume a file stays available after you leave the chat or the room expires.

about.title: Why a wallet here?
body: BURN is a token on the TON network. The wallet shows your on-chain BURN balance and lets you send BURN to others in chat.
You also need a small amount of native {{symbol}} on the same wallet to pay network fees for transfers.
Your keys stay in your TON wallet app — Burned Chats reads balances and builds transactions; it cannot spend without your approval.
Burning a chat (Burn chat) permanently deletes that conversation. It does not burn BURN tokens.
Ordinary BURN transfers burn 0.5% of the amount on-chain (fee-on-transfer). That permanently reduces network circulating supply. Fee-burn does not create a Burn BURN row in this wallet history.
Open How BURN works under your balance for the token explainer — fee-burn, staking, and governance.
After mint is closed, the wallet also shows how much of the 1000 BURN cap has been burned.
You can also voluntarily burn BURN you hold (not staked) with a TEP-74 JettonBurn on your jetton wallet. That is not a transfer to a burn address. It cannot be undone.
The connected wallet is the TON Connect session on this device. Send, stake, and vote use that key, and the balances shown belong to it — not to an account-wide pot.
The linked wallet is the address stored on your Burned Chats account. If they differ, make the connected key primary or disconnect this session.
Compare these build-time contract addresses with an independent source. A CDN-compromised app could show different values.

Staking master: {{pinnedStaking}}
Governor: {{pinnedGovernor}}
Treasury: {{pinnedTreasury}}
